description: Component upgrade lifecycle for the AI platform. This file lives on the `lifecycle` branch
(the GitHub default branch, so Renovate reads it from here) and targets `main` only.
`main` carries NO Renovate annotations: every pin is found by the managers below, keyed on
the shapes that exist on `main` today. tests/test_renovate_coverage.py (run weekly against
`main` by .github/workflows/coverage.yaml) fails when a pin stops matching.
PRs are grouped by UPGRADE DOMAIN, each anchored on the component whose version gates the
others (see COMPATIBILITY.md):
infra      - anchored on the EKS Kubernetes version (Karpenter, LBC, KEDA, TF modules/providers, k8s clients)
inference  - anchored on the vLLM image (gpu-operator, GIE CRDs, llm-d router, s5cmd, prometheus)
gateway    - LiteLLM and what talks to it (postgres, langfuse, open-webui, oauth2-proxy, python libs)
gitops     - ArgoCD / KRO (self-managed path)
tooling    - GitHub Actions + CI tool versions
What waits, and for what (COMPATIBILITY.md, 'Anchors, and what waits'): majors need a tick on the
Dependency Dashboard; the EKS Kubernetes version is proposed 60 days after the minor's release;
vLLM changes and LiteLLM minors when the version is 14 days old; kro and llm-d router minors at
once on their own branch. Everything else flows with its group. EKS managed add-ons are not
managed here: Terraform takes the newest build (most_recent = true) and addon-freshness on
`main` reports drift.
Merge policy: nothing automerges and Renovate PRs into `main` are never merged directly; their
branches are merged into a `release/<version>` branch, validated by E2E, and merged together.

customManagers.description: Helm charts declared in the ArgoCD platform ApplicationSet (chart / chartRepo / chartVersion triplets).

vLLM serving image default baked into the KRO serving-tier schemas (VLLMEndpoint, LLMDEndpoint, LLMDDisaggEndpoint). Must track terraform/30.eks/30.cluster/locals.tf vllm_image_tag; same group so they move together.
llm-d router Helm chart (OCI, ghcr.io/llm-d/charts) default in the LLMD* KRO schemas.
Python base image used by the Platform Health Agent's spawned Jobs (a ConfigMap value, not an image: field). An optional @digest is tracked too (rebuilds with OS fixes).

Inline 'pip install name==version' pins inside init containers (litellm-sync, cluster-dashboard, PHA event-watcher) AND inside the Job specs the dashboard/PHA Python builds at runtime (backend.py, event_watcher.py). Those Jobs run on PYTHON_IMAGE, so a python bump needs wheels for these pins.
vLLM serving image tag, single source of truth in the cluster stage locals (vllm_image_tag = "<v>"). Same dep as the RGD defaults, so both move in one PR.

AWS Load Balancer Controller chart: lbc_chart_version = "<v>" in terraform/30.eks/35.addons/main.tf (one pin for the chart and its CRDs). The older shape, chart_version = "<v>" inside the aws_load_balancer_controller block, is still matched for releases cut before that change.
Python CI tools pinned inline in workflow run steps (`pip install [flags] name==v name==v ...`). Recursive: first the pip line, then each name==version on it.
kustomize release tarball in CI (`KUSTOMIZE_VERSION="<v>"` shell assignment).

EKS Kubernetes version (anchor): cluster_config.kubernetes_version in the example tfvars, the default for new clusters. Source: endoflife.date (amazon-eks). Proposed 60 days after the minor's release, one minor at a time (see packageRules).

Karpenter chart: karpenter_chart_version = "<v>" in terraform/30.eks/30.cluster/karpenter.tf, one pin for the chart and its CRDs (the helm_release reads it from the local, which the built-in terraform manager cannot see).

kro chart (self-managed): kro_chart_version = "<v>" in capabilities-selfmanaged.tf, one pin for the chart and its CRDs (main #58). The helm_release reads the local, which the built-in terraform manager cannot see.

Argo CD's Redis image: argocd_redis_image = "<tag>@<digest>" in capabilities-selfmanaged.tf overrides the argo-cd chart's fixed Redis tag, whose Alpine packages are never refreshed (Critical CVEs on dev, 2026-11-16). The digest makes Renovate also propose rebuilds of the same tag (Alpine security fixes). Docker Hub's redis has the same digests as the chart's ecr-public mirror.

Images in the Langfuse chart's values (Valkey, SeaweedFS) written as repository + tag "<tag>@<digest>": the sub-charts' defaults are floating tags, pinned here so Renovate proposes new versions and rebuilds.

packageRules.description: The built-in terraform manager also reports a helm_release whose version is a reference such as ${local.karpenter_chart_version}; the literal behind it is read by a regex manager. Skip the reference so it is never looked up or rewritten.
Default: every Terraform provider/module is infra (control-plane adjacent). Later rules override for specific deps.
infra domain - anchored on the EKS Kubernetes version. Karpenter chart<->CRD<->k8s window, LBC v3 (CRDs applied separately + IAM supplement), KEDA, k8s clients.
k8s Python client must stay within +/-1 minor of the API server (kubernetes-client policy). Ceiling = (EKS default minor + 2), exclusive; raise it by hand with the EKS anchor.
alpine/k8s bundles kubectl; keep within +/-1 minor of the API server (kubectl skew policy). Ceiling = 1.(EKS default minor + 2), exclusive; raise it by hand with the EKS anchor.
inference domain - anchored on the vLLM image. GPU operator driver/CUDA >= vLLM's CUDA runtime; GIE CRDs + llm-d router must match the vLLM routing protocol.

gateway domain - LiteLLM and everything that talks to it. Postgres major = dump/restore; Langfuse chart v2->v3 = ClickHouse data-store migration. Langfuse 4 stores (ClickHouse >= 25.12, Valkey, SeaweedFS) move with Langfuse.
gitops domain - the engine that applies everything else (self-managed ESC path; managed capabilities are AWS-owned).
tooling domain - CI only, no cluster impact.
Anything found in a GitHub workflow is CI-only, whatever its dep name (python, pyyaml, kubernetes... also exist cluster-side). File-based so it overrides the dep-name groups above.

LiteLLM: follow its long-term-support releases (vX.Y.Z-lts). Until May 2026 LiteLLM published '-stable' tags (last v1.83.14-stable.patch.3) and this rule followed those, so Renovate proposed nothing for six months after LiteLLM switched. The versioning reads both shapes, so the current '-stable' pin compares with the '-lts' tags; nightlies, dev and rc tags never match.

Majors anywhere: nothing is proposed until a human ticks the checkbox on the Dependency Dashboard, so an open major PR means 'approved for the next cycle'. Majors are the one kind of update that stays with a person: they usually need code changes or a data migration. Closing the PR takes the approval back; recreateWhen=always makes Renovate offer it again on the dashboard instead of treating the close as 'never'.

vLLM runs every user's model; under 0.x each minor can drop architectures or change flags users set in extraArgs, and E2E serves one small model. Its own branch, so it never holds back the rest of the inference group. No dashboard tick: nobody is assigned to tick. The update is proposed by itself, on its own branch, once the version is 14 days old (minimumReleaseAge; the registry gives release dates, and a version without a date is held, never proposed early). The factory takes at most one anchor update (vLLM, EKS version) per cycle, tests it like everything else, and forkers get it only with the next published release.

kro's ResourceGraphDefinitions (VLLMEndpoint, LLMDEndpoint) are the API users write model manifests against. It is 0.x, where a minor may break that contract: minors get their own branch, so a failure blames them alone; patches flow with their group. No dashboard tick and no release age: this registry gives Renovate no release dates, and an age without a date would hold the update forever. E2E judges it (kro expands a VLLMEndpoint, llm-d routes and scales), and forkers get it only with the next published release, after weeks of cycles.

llm-d router: same rule as kro (0.x; a minor can change how users' llm-d traffic is routed). Minors get their own branch; patches flow with the inference group. No dashboard tick and no release age: this registry gives Renovate no release dates, and an age without a date would hold the update forever. E2E judges it (kro expands a VLLMEndpoint, llm-d routes and scales), and forkers get it only with the next published release, after weeks of cycles.

LiteLLM is the gateway every user's requests, keys, budgets and spend go through, and its minors change proxy behaviour and the database schema (1.83 -> 1.108 in 2026). Minors get their own branch, so a jump never rides along with the gateway group; LTS patches flow with the group. No dashboard tick: nobody is assigned to tick. The update is proposed by itself, on its own branch, once the version is 14 days old (minimumReleaseAge; the registry gives release dates, and a version without a date is held, never proposed early). The factory takes at most one anchor update (vLLM, EKS version) per cycle, tests it like everything else, and forkers get it only with the next published release.

The github-actions manager also reads setup-terraform's terraform_version (depName 'terraform'). The regex manager above owns that pin (depName hashicorp/terraform, same as the terraform manager), so disable the built-in copy to avoid two PRs for one line.

EKS Kubernetes anchor: its own branch and PR. endoflife.date lists versions as 1.37-eks-N; keep the minor only. A release may add at most one minor above the previous release (release.py enforces it), so each newer minor is listed separately (separateMultipleMinor). Raise the alpine/k8s and kubernetes-client allowedVersions ceilings in the same release (tests/test_renovate_coverage.py pairs them). No dashboard tick: nobody is assigned to tick. The update is proposed by itself, on its own branch, once the version is 60 days old (minimumReleaseAge; the registry gives release dates, and a version without a date is held, never proposed early). The factory takes at most one anchor update (vLLM, EKS version) per cycle, tests it like everything else, and forkers get it only with the next published release.
Langfuse's ClickHouse stays on LTS lines (x.3 and x.8, a year of fixes); the monthly releases in between get about three months. Langfuse 4 needs 25.12 or newer.
